payload.title: Rust rewrite: backend + core framework (v0.4.0)
payload.description:
Big-bang rewrite of everything server-side and toolchain into Rust. Only the web client (packages/core + packages/react + apps/web), the Swift SDK, and the Kotlin SDK stay in their current languages.

## Decisions (locked with Bri 2026-06-09)

- **Strategy:** big-bang — build the Rust replacement to full parity in a new tree, then cut over and delete the TS backend in one release (v0.4.0).
- **Wire compatibility:** hard requirement. The Rust server is a drop-in at the protocol layer: same MessagePack frame protocol, schema identity (schemaId/Version/Revision/Hash), and structured error envelope. Existing Swift/Kotlin/web clients must work unchanged.
- **TS client runtime stays:** packages/core + packages/react are treated as part of the web client and remain TypeScript.
- **Schema authoring:** moves to a Rust DSL/macros. TypeScript becomes a generated codegen target alongside Swift and Kotlin. Canonical schema AST semantics and hashing must be preserved so schema identity is stable across the rewrite.
- **App authoring after cutover:** both modes — embed Frick as a Rust library (schema + server wiring in Rust, like today's server.ts) AND a standalone `frick-server` binary that loads compiled schema artifacts + config.
- **Storage:** SQLite first (same durable+cache store port semantics), and this epic also lands the Postgres runtime store as a first-class backend (finishes the FR-4 direction in Rust). Local SQLite DBs are disposable; no data migration.
- **Stack:** tokio + axum/hyper (HTTP + WebSocket), rmp-serde (MessagePack), rusqlite + sqlx/tokio-postgres, tracing. Boring and well-supported.
- **Repo layout:** Cargo workspace (crates/) added to this monorepo alongside the pnpm workspace. TS backend deleted at cutover; web client + generated TS stay.
- **Acceptance:** a language-neutral conformance suite (wire fixtures + black-box scenario tests) run against BOTH servers until cutover, plus the three client SDK suites passing against the Rust server.
- **Scope includes:** apps/server, packages/protocol (as Rust crate), schema codegen, apps/cli, packages/mcp + packages/agent-kit, apps/rangercrm-server (dogfood). dev-dashboard/devtools/design stay TS.
- **Parity bar:** ALL of it — objects, streams, presence, signals, projections, jobs, blobs, sharing grants, cluster bus + Redis adapter, push adapters (APNs/FCM + per-tenant creds + telemetry), admin/inspection routes + dashboard API.

## Sequencing

Foundation (workspace, protocol crate, schema DSL, codegen, storage) → server core → primitives → distributed/ops surfaces → conformance + SDK acceptance → tooling (CLI/MCP/rangercrm) → cutover PR that deletes the TS backend and ships v0.4.0.
